\begin{lemma}[Probability after a fixed run segment]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_seg}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_seg}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_drop, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_append}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine and $C,C'$ configurations on the same fixed
input. Suppose every choice word of length $S$ takes $C$ to $C'$. For any
$T\in\mathbb{N}$ and decidable configuration property $Q$, the probability that $Q$
holds after a uniformly chosen length-$(S+T)$ run from $C$ equals the probability that
it holds after a uniformly chosen length-$T$ run from $C'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Probability at a binary choice]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_choose}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_choose}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_succ, Turing.Cfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.runWith_cons, Turing.NDTM.stepWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine and $C$ a configuration on a fixed input.
Suppose its one-step successor from $C$ under choice bit $b$ is $C_b$ for each
$b\in\{0,1\}$. For any $T\in\mathbb{N}$ and decidable configuration property $Q$, the
probability that $Q$ holds after $T+1$ uniformly chosen steps from $C$ is the average of
the probabilities that $Q$ holds after $T$ uniformly chosen steps from $C_1$ and from
$C_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Run probability after halting]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_mono}

Let $M$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine and $C$ an initial configuration. Suppose
every choice word of length $T$ leads to a halted configuration, and let $T\le T'$. For

uniformly chosen length-$T'$ run from $C$ equals the probability for a uniformly chosen

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One-step randomization invariance]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_narun_det}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.randProb_narun_det}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.NARM.detPart, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.narun, Complexity.LogProg.narun_cons, Complexity.LogProg.nastep_det, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_succ}
\difficulty{4}
Let a nondeterministic register machine with $m$ registers and $d$ Boolean oracles have
state set $\Lambda$, input $x$, and oracle $O$. Suppose its instruction at state $l$ is
the deterministic instruction $i$. For any bit $\beta$, register valuation $v$, stored
answer $r$, and decidable configuration property $R$, the probability that $R$ holds
after running for $N+1$ uniformly chosen bits from $(l,v,r)$ equals the probability that
it holds after taking the deterministic step at $l$ and then running for $N$ uniformly
chosen bits.
\end{lemma}

of the corresponding fractions of length-$N$ choice strings starting from $l_1$ and
$l_0$.
\end{lemma}

state set $\Lambda$, input $x$, initial configuration $a$, and let $G$ be a

property $R$, the probability that $R$ holds after a uniformly chosen length-$N'$ choice
word equals the corresponding probability for a uniformly chosen length-$N$ choice word.
\end{lemma}

Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with initial label $l_0$, oracle, and
decider machine $D$ with initial states $q_0$ and space bound $B$. Fix an input $x$,
register values $v$, output prefix $out$, and natural numbers $W,N$. Suppose every
sequence of $N$ choice bits makes the program halt, and each configuration before
halting satisfies the guard: its applicable instruction preconditions hold, every
decider call has distinct argument registers and a clean run using at most $B$ work-head
cells, and each register value $z$ satisfies $|	ext{the binary length of }z+1|\le W$.

of length-$N$ sequences on which the register program's final answer is $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compiled and Program Acceptance Probabilities]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_randProb}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_randProb}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NGuard, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.aseam, Complexity.LogProg.narm_run_randProb, Complexity.LogProg.narun, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileFinNDTM, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileTM, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileTM_init, Complexity.LogProg.randProb_runWith_mono, Complexity.LogProg.seam, Randomized.randProb, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,d,k_D,N,T$ be nonnegative integers, let $\Lambda$ and $SD$ be finite sets, let
$A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle choices,
and let $l_0$ be its initial location. Fix an input bit string $x$, an oracle assigning
a Boolean answer to each of the $d$ indices and each bit string, a deterministic
$k_D$-tape machine $D$, a choice of initial state $q_0(j)$ for each oracle index, and
bounds $B,W$. Suppose every length-$N$ choice string makes the program halt, and every
configuration before halting satisfies the guard requiring its deterministic
preconditions and register bit-length bounds by $W$. If the compiled nondeterministic
machine halts on $x$ after every choice string of length $T$, then for each Boolean
value $b$, the probability that a uniformly chosen length-$T$ choice string makes the
compiled machine output exactly $b$ equals the probability that a uniformly chosen
length-$N$ choice string makes the register program return $b$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_randProb_accept}

a Boolean answer to each of the $d$ indices and each bit string, a deterministic
$k_D$-tape machine $D$, a choice of initial state $q_0(j)$ for each oracle index, and
bounds $B,W$. Suppose every length-$N$ choice string makes the program halt, and every
configuration before halting satisfies the guard requiring its deterministic
preconditions and register bit-length bounds by $W$. If the compiled nondeterministic

\begin{theorem}[Space and probability preservation under compilation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.narm_space_randProb}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.narm_space_randProb}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NGuard, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.narm_randProb, Complexity.LogProg.narm_space, Complexity.LogProg.narun, Complexity.LogProg.ncompileFinNDTM, Randomized.randProb, Turing.FinNDTM.AcceptsWithin, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.NDTM.HaltsWithin, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.NDTM.spaceUsedWith}
\difficulty{1}
Let $m,d,k_D,N$ be nonnegative integers, let $A$ be a nondeterministic register
machine with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle indices, let $x$ be a bit string, let
$	ext{oracle}$ assign a Boolean answer to each oracle index and bit string, and let $D$
be a deterministic Turing machine with $k_D$ work tapes. Suppose the register machine
halts after $N$ choice bits on every choice string of length $N$, with every
configuration before halting satisfying the guard that each register has binary length
at most $W$ and every oracle call is clean and uses at most $B$ work-tape cells per head
position. Then there is a time bound $T$ such that the compiled nondeterministic Turing
machine halts on every choice string of length $T$, uses at most $m(W+2)+k_D(2B+1)$
work-tape cells on each such run, and accepts within $T$ steps exactly when the register
machine can produce result true after $N$ choices. Moreover, for each Boolean value $b$,
the fraction of length-$T$ choice strings on which the compiled machine outputs exactly
$b$ equals the fraction of length-$N$ choice strings on which the register machine's
result is $b$.
\end{theorem}
